report:
This claim is accurate and well-supported by regulatory and clinical evidence.

**FDA Approval:** The U.S. FDA approved Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) specifically "for prevention of pregnancy for up to five years," as confirmed in Bayer's official approval announcement (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html) and corroborated in the drug approval history record (https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html).

**FDA Prescribing Label:** The official FDA-approved label on DailyMed states plainly: "Kyleena should not remain in the uterus after 5 years" (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080), directly confirming the five-year approved duration for contraceptive use.

**Clinical evidence base:** The five-year indication rests on Phase III trial data (approximately 1,452 healthy women aged 18–35) demonstrating sustained contraceptive efficacy (low Pearl Index, i.e., pregnancy rate per 100 woman-years) across the full five-year period, as reflected in prescriber materials summarizing "cumulative efficacy over 5 years" (https://www.kyleenahcp.com/media/2276/download).

**Context/comparison:** Kyleena is one of several levonorgestrel IUDs with differing hormone doses and approved durations—Skyla (13.5 mg, 3 years), Mirena and Liletta (52 mg, up to 8 years)—with Kyleena's 19.5 mg dose positioned as the lowest-dose option among 5-year systems, consistent across multiple independent comparison sources.

**Conclusion:** The claim is true and consistent across the manufacturer, FDA labeling, and clinical trial evidence: Kyleena is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years. No credible source contradicts this; some sources note that off-label extended use beyond 5 years has been studied for other similar IUDs, but Kyleena's approved label remains capped at 5 years.
